items.title: INNOZHERO: A major step towards capturing carbon emissions from waste
items.summary: CINEA reports that the INNOZHERO carbon capture project in Helsingborg, Sweden, has reached its Final Investment Decision. It is described as one of Europe's first large-scale carbon capture facilities at a waste-to-energy plant and is supported by the EU Innovation Fund.
items.why_it_matters: A firm new Swedish capture source moves to FID, adding confirmed volume to southern-Sweden CO2 flows that need port, shipping and storage capacity.

items.title: First process equipment installed at Beccs Stockholm
items.summary: Stockholm Exergi reports that the first process equipment has been installed at Beccs Stockholm, its bio-CCS plant under construction. The company describes this as another construction milestone for the project.
items.why_it_matters: Beccs Stockholm is one of the largest planned Nordic biogenic CO2 sources; construction progress informs timing assumptions for Baltic Sea shipping and storage capacity.

items.title: Norway supports CCUS development in Poland
items.summary: Poland is the largest recipient of EEA and Norway Grants for 2021-2028, with €924.9 million allocated, including €160.9 million through the Green Transition Programme. Gassnova is contributing Norwegian CCS expertise and experience to CCUS development in Poland under this programme.
items.why_it_matters: Norwegian support for Polish CCUS could shape future Baltic Sea CO2 source volumes and cross-border shipping demand towards North Sea storage.

items.title: Industry perspectives on CO2 transport optimization models and case studies
items.summary: Paper in Computers & Industrial Engineering by Stephan Bogs, Ali Abdelshafy and Grit Walther. As its title states, it presents industry perspectives on CO2 transport optimization models and case studies.
items.why_it_matters: Directly addresses how practitioners view CO2 transport optimisation models, useful for validating model assumptions in Nordic network design studies.
items.authors: Stephan Bogs, Ali Abdelshafy, Grit Walther

items.title: A novel approach for preliminary sizing and cost screening of CO2 pipeline transport: The ECOB method
items.source: International journal of greenhouse gas control
items.summary: The study develops an Economic Operating Band (ECOB)-based framework for rapid CO2 pipeline sizing and transport cost screening. It targets early-stage CCS chain assessments where detailed diameter-by-diameter hydraulic optimisation is hard to embed and simple sizing rules miss the trade-off between investment and operating costs.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a fast pipeline sizing and cost-screening method that could be embedded in network optimisation models comparing pipeline and ship options.
items.authors: Binxu Gao, Nicola Zecca, Giampaolo Manzolini

items.title: Biomass as a transportable biogenic carbon carrier for e-methanol production: Techno-economic comparison with CO2 transport and direct air capture
items.summary: Paper in Biomass and Bioenergy by Namdarpour Naghani, Galimova, Mensah, Koiranen and Breyer. As its title states, it compares transporting biomass as a biogenic carbon carrier for e-methanol production with CO2 transport and direct air capture in a techno-economic analysis.
items.why_it_matters: Provides an alternative to CO2 transport (moving biomass instead of CO2), relevant when weighing transport mode and supply-chain configuration for biogenic CO2 in the Nordics.
items.authors: Sina Namdarpour Naghani, Tansu Galimova, Theophilus Nii Odai Mensah, Tuomas Koiranen, Christian Breyer

items.title: Toward lower-cost carbon capture, utilization, and storage: Fit-for-purpose CO2 conditioning and source–sink coordination
items.summary: Paper in Petroleum Science by Hai-Zhu Wang and co-authors. As its title states, it addresses lowering CCUS costs through fit-for-purpose CO2 conditioning and source–sink coordination.
items.why_it_matters: Source–sink matching and CO2 quality specifications are core inputs to CCS network design and cost optimisation.
items.authors: Hai-Zhu Wang, Yao-Chen Zhang, Bin Wang, Bo-Xin Ding, Jing-Yang Pu, Sergey Stanchits et al.

items.title: Sustainable closed-loop supply chain network planning with CCUS: A multi-objective robust optimization framework under two carbon policies
items.summary: Paper in the International Journal of Production Economics by Song Xu, Yuting Xie, Wenting Yang and Lu Liu. As its title states, it proposes a multi-objective robust optimisation framework for sustainable closed-loop supply chain network planning with CCUS under two carbon policies.
items.why_it_matters: Shows robust optimisation methods for supply-chain network planning that integrate CCUS under alternative carbon policy regimes, applicable to policy-scenario analysis.
items.authors: Song Xu, Yuting Xie, Wenting Yang, Lu Liu
